examples.purpose: Recent transactions on a home screen, the guide's In context: the drawer peeks under Home (140 px here) with its title and the first transaction. People drag it or press its handle to expand it, and the screen's See all transactions button opens it too. The screen keeps the drawer's state in its own state: the button sets it to expanded, and onStateChange reports drags and handle presses for the screen to apply back. The literal state and the empty handlers here are placeholders for that wiring. The drawer fills the Screen it sits in.
examples.jsx:
<Screen>
  <VStack alignHorizontal="center">
    <Text text="Home" />
    <Button label="See all transactions" onPress={() => {}} />
  </VStack>
  <Drawer
    title="Recent transactions"
    collapsedHeight={140}
    state="collapsed"
    onStateChange={() => {}}
  >
    <ListGroup>
      <ListItem layout="Horizontal" title="Netflix" supportText="25 March · 17:30" trailing={<MoneyValue value="500" currency="₹" />} onPress={() => {}} />
      <ListItem layout="Horizontal" title="Spotify" supportText="24 March · 09:12" trailing={<MoneyValue value="119" currency="₹" />} onPress={() => {}} />
      <ListItem layout="Horizontal" title="Amazon" supportText="22 March · 21:04" trailing={<MoneyValue value="1,299" currency="₹" />} onPress={() => {}} />
    </ListGroup>
  </Drawer>
</Screen>

from.quote: The drawer peeks under the home screen. People drag it or press its handle to expand it, and the screen’s See all transactions button opens it too.

examples.purpose: With a scrim, the guide's Configuration: the screen dims behind the expanded drawer and taps on it don't get through. A press on the scrim calls onOverlayPress, which the package says is typically used to collapse the drawer: here the screen would set its state back to collapsed. The literal state and the empty handlers are placeholders for the screen's own state.

props.name: modes
props.description: The drawer's modes are not passed to its children: every child needs its own modes.

props.name: header
props.description: Fixed header content that remains visible and does not scroll. Placed immediately after the handle.

props.name: collapsedHeight
props.description: How much of the sheet shows when collapsed, in px (default 200). The drawer sizes from its parent (the host layer's onLayout), not the window: 140 shows 140 px and 200 shows 200; with the default expandedRatio, expanded is 0.9 of the parent's height.

props.name: expandedRatio
props.description: How tall the drawer is when expanded, as a ratio: default 0.9, clamped to 0.2–0.95.

props.name: initialState
props.description: The state at mount when state is not given (default collapsed). Declared: Sets the drawer state when it first mounts (uncontrolled mode). Ignored once `state` is provided (controlled mode).

props.name: state
props.description: A controlled state applies at mount: state="expanded" renders expanded. Declared: Programmatically controls the drawer's collapsed/expanded state. When provided, the drawer becomes a controlled component: it will animate to match this value (reusing the same spring used by gestures) and gesture-driven changes are reported via `onStateChange` for the parent to apply back. Leave undefined for uncontrolled behaviour.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: The dialog's name. The sheet is a dialog named accessibilityLabel, then title, then “Drawer”.

props.name: bottomInset
props.description: Extra bottom inset (in px) added to the scroll content so that items at the very bottom remain visible above overlapping UI such as a tab bar. Defaults to 80.

props.name: onStateChange
props.description: Called whenever the drawer settles into a new state (collapsed or expanded), so parent components can react programmatically.

props.name: showOverlay
props.description: A static rgba(0,0,0,0.7) scrim behind the sheet, shown in both states; without onOverlayPress it still blocks taps on the screen. Declared: When `true`, renders a full-screen semi-transparent {@link Overlay} scrim behind the drawer sheet (dimming everything else on screen). Defaults to `false`, in which case nothing is rendered behind the sheet and behaviour is unchanged.

props.name: onOverlayPress
props.description: Called when the overlay scrim (the area outside the sheet) is pressed. Only relevant when `showOverlay` is `true` — typically used to collapse or dismiss the drawer.

modes.name: Color Mode
modes.description: A token collection Drawer reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.

modes.name: Page type
modes.description: A token collection Drawer reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.

slots.name: header
slots.description: Fixed header content that remains visible and does not scroll. Placed immediately after the handle.

events.name: onStateChange
events.description: Called whenever the drawer settles into a new state (collapsed or expanded), so parent components can react programmatically.

events.name: onOverlayPress
events.description: Called when the overlay scrim (the area outside the sheet) is pressed. Only relevant when `showOverlay` is `true` — typically used to collapse or dismiss the drawer.
